significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that backtracking is causally implemented by an ordered two-stage mechanism in which “an error/inconsistency detector writes a signal that suppresses the current reasoning path and up-weights alternative continuations,” and that this mechanism strengthens through RL; this is form (iii) insofar as it fixes a computational ordering and training-stage dependence, supported by form-(ii) causal claims about correction and looping. DeepSeek-R1 (Guo et al., 2025) treats reflection and alternative exploration as characteristic RL-emergent behavior, while s1 (Muennighoff et al., 2025) shows that manipulating “Wait” and reasoning budgets affects performance, so the proposed conclusion would materially constrain why those behavioral and efficiency effects occur rather than merely identify a backtracking representation. It establishes both a phenomenon—RL-associated emergence of productive backtracking—and a mechanism separating detection from rerouting, with consequences for useful correction and wasteful loops; a negative result would rule out this unified ordered account, although the compound hypothesis would not by itself identify which stage or RL-emergence premise failed. True and false outcomes are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check passes: deleting the detect-then-reroute ordering and RL-emergence relation leaves only generic efficient-reasoning interpretability, which would not warrant this above-median score.

reach.justification: The concrete handles are the claim’s “detector-direction” and “detector-gated correction,” which could be used to stimulate correction when a partial reasoning path becomes inconsistent or suppress the same pathway to reduce “wasteful loops.” This is ex ante relative to the final answer and token overrun: the detector fires during reasoning, leaving an action window to reroute or stop before the eventual failure or excess computation. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive conclusion predicts an ordered detector-to-rerouter coupling and stronger circuitry in RL-trained than base models, rather than supplying only an open-ended search procedure; the asserted scope is RL-trained reasoners generally, and downstream users could include model builders or deployment practitioners controlling accuracy-token tradeoffs. The topic-substitution check passes because generic mechanism-based efficient reasoning supplies neither this detector signal nor a gating intervention, so the reach score comes from the claim-specific transferable relation and control handle rather than the topic’s importance.
